The aim was to investigate the impact of climate change on the growth and development of maize in different regions of Kenya. The researchers collected data on various factors, including temperature, rainfall, and soil type, to assess the relationship between these factors and maize yield. The results showed that climate change has a significant impact on maize production in Kenya, and that some regions are more vulnerable than others.

The study also examined the potential of using drought-resistant maize varieties to mitigate the negative effects of climate change. The researchers found that drought-resistant maize varieties can significantly increase maize yield, especially in regions that are prone to drought.

The study provides valuable information for farmers and policymakers in Kenya, and can help them to make informed decisions about maize production and climate change adaptation strategies.

samples.ref: Ohun èlò àti ìlànà:
samples.hyp:
The study was conducted in a rural area of Oyo State, Nigeria. A total of 800 participants were recruited, comprising 400 males and 400 females, aged 18-55 years. Data was collected using a structured questionnaire.

Results
The mean age of the participants was 35.2 years. The prevalence of hypertension was 25.5%.

Discussion
Hypertension is a major public health problem in Nigeria. This study provides further evidence that hypertension is associated with older age.

samples.src: The current study was conducted to investigate the reproductive toxicity of sodium metavanadate (SMV) in male African giant rats.
samples.ref: Ìwádìí lọ́ọ́lọ́ náà jẹ́ ṣíṣe láti ṣe ìwádìí iwọ ìbísí ti sódíọ́mù mẹtafẹ́nádéètì (SMV) nínú àwọn akọ òkété.
samples.hyp: The study aimed to determine the dose levels that could cause adverse effects on the reproductive system of the rats.

samples.src: Administration of SMV was done intraperitoneally daily for 14 consecutive days at a dosage of 3mg/kg body weight.
samples.ref: Ìṣákóso SMV jẹ́ ṣíṣe pẹ̀lú gbígba abẹ́rẹ́ sínú lójoojúmọ́ fún ọjọ́ 14 lérawọn pẹ̀lú ìwọ̀n 3 mg/kg fún ìlóòrìn ara.

samples.src: Sterile water was administered to the control group.
samples.ref: Omi tí kò lábàwọ́n jẹ́ lílò ní ọ̀wọ́ àyẹ̀wò.
samples.hyp: The control group consisted of 100 animals. The animals in the control group did not show any signs of the disease.

samples.src: We analyzed serum reproductive hormones, sperm reserve and quality as well as testicular ultrastructural changes following SMV treatment.
samples.ref: A ṣe àtúpalẹ̀ àwọn hòmóònù ìbísí omi ara, ìpamọ̣́ àti ìwọ̀n ìdára àtọ̀ tí ó fi mọ́ àwọn ìyípada ipò ẹpọ̀n nínú láti ara itọju SMV.

samples.src: Our results showed SMV exposed AGR group had statistically increased progesterone but decreased testosterone, FSH and LH concentrations.

samples.src: Also, SMV treated group had statistically decreased sperm motility and mass activity with increased percentage of abnormal morphophenotypes of spermatozoa and upregulation of P53 immunopositive cell.

samples.src: Ultrastructural study revealed vocuolation of germ and Sertoli cells, cytoplasmic and nucleus; and mitochondrial swelling and vacuolations were also observed.

samples.src: There was severe disintegration of the seminiferous tubules, atrophy and degeneration of myeloid cells and apoptosis of the Leydig, Sertoli and germ cells.

samples.src: In conclusion, intraperitoneal SMV exposure exerts severe adverse effects on some serum reproductive hormones, reduction of sperm reserve and quality, apoptosis and degenerative changes of the Leydig, Sertoli and germ cells which can lead to infertility.

samples.hyp: The vanadium concentration in the injected rats was 100 μg/kg body weight. The researchers then examined the rats' brains to see if there were any changes.

samples.src: At the same time, they injected another 6 rats with water as a “control” experiment.

samples.src: Using a technique called Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), they were able to see any changes that occurred in the testicles in detail, down to the level of individual cells.

samples.src: Cultural Use of Homegarden Plants in an Indigenous Community in North West Ethiopia
samples.ref: Ìlò ajẹmáṣà àwọn Ewéko Ọgbà-etílé ní àwọn Àdúgbò Ìjímìjí ní Àríwá-Ìwọ̀-oorùn Ethiopia.

samples.src: The floristic composition of homegardens in Northwest Ethiopia in general, and the Gozamin district in particular, has received little research attention.
samples.ref: Àkójọpọ̀ gbogbo ẹ̀yà ewéko fún àwọn ọgbà-etílé ní Àríwá Ìwọ̀-oorùn Ethiopia, àti pàápàá jù lọ agbègbè Gozamin ti rí ìfojúsí ìwádìí díè.

samples.src: The purpose of this research is to better understand the floristic composition and cultural significance of homegardens.
samples.ref: Ìdí fún ìwádìí yìí ní láti mọ àmọ̀dunjú àkójọpọ̀ gbogbo ẹ̀yà ewéko àti ìdí ajẹmáṣà pàtó àwọn ọ̀gbà-etílé.

samples.src: Stratified random sampling procedure was used based on agroecological variation in selected kebeles.
samples.ref: Ìlànà yíyan àpẹẹrẹ láti ara àwọn ọ̀wọ́ ohun abèmí́ kọ̀ọ̀kan láti dá ọ̀wọ́ míràn sílẹ̀ ni wọ́n lò látàrí ìṣoríṣiríṣi ohun abẹ̀mí tó ń ran nǹkan ọ̀gbìn lọ́wọ́ ní àwọn kebéíle tí wọ́n yàn.

samples.src: The homegarden data were collected by dividing the homegarden into four quadrats, the first quadrat stretched from the farmer’s home to 10m, the second quadrat from10m to 20m, the third quadrat from 20m to 30m and the fourth quadrat from 30m to 40m horizontally using farmer’s house as reference depending on the size of the garden.
samples.ref: Dátà ọgbà-etílé náà jẹ́ gbígbà látàrí pípín àwọn ọgbà-etílé náà sí mẹ́rin,ìpin àkọ́kọ́ wá láti ilé àgbẹ̀ náà sí 10m, ìpí kejì wá láti 10m sí 20m, ìpín kẹta wá láti 20m sí 30m, ìpín kẹrin sì wá láti 30m sí 40m níla pẹ̀tẹ́lẹ̀ tí a bá lo ilé àgbẹ̀ náà gẹ́gẹ́ bíi ìtọ́kasí, èyí tó dá lé bí ọ̀gbà-etílé náà ṣe tóbi sí.

samples.src: A semi-structured interview was carried out to document the informant’s knowledge on plant species.
samples.ref: Ìfọ̀rọ̀wánilẹ́nuwò elétò-ráńpé wáyé láti ṣe ìkọsílẹ̀ ìmọ̀ alálàyé lórí àwọn ẹ̀yà ewéko.

samples.src: A total of 238 culturally important plant species from 81 families were identified.
samples.ref: Àkójọ ẹ̀yà àwọn 238 ewéko ìjímìjí pàtàkì láti ẹbí 81 ni wọ́n ṣe ìdánimọ̀ fún.
samples.hyp: The most common families were the Poaceae (grasses) with 42 species, followed by the Fabaceae (legumes) with 35 species, and the Asteraceae (sunflowers) with 28 species.

samples.src: Of these 39% were herbs,29% shrubs, 6% were climbers.
samples.ref: Lára wọn 39% jẹ́ ẹgbòogi, 29% jẹ́ àwọn igi kékèké, 6% sì jẹ́ àwọn ewéko agùn.
samples.hyp: The remaining 26% were trees.

samples.src: Perennials made up the largest part of cultivated species (83%), whereas annuals made up the rest (17%).
samples.ref: Àwọn ewéko ọlọ́jọ́ pípẹ́ ló pọ̀ jù nínú àwọn ẹ̀yà tí wọ́n gbìn (83%), tí ìyókù sì jẹ́ àwọn ọlọ́dọọdún (17%).
samples.hyp: The study also showed that the most common species were those that are native to the region.

samples.src: The Poaceae family had the foremost species, with 22, taken after by the Fabaceae, which had 21, and the Asteraceae which had 15.

samples.hyp: The most common species were those of the genus *Panicum*, followed by *Digitaria* and *Cenchrus*.

samples.src: From these recorded plants,140 (58.6%) were species utilized for environmental uses, 84 (35%) food crops, 83 (34.7%) medicinal plant species, 39 (16.3%) fodder species, 57 (23.8%) material use plants, 60 (25%) fuel wood species, 50(21%) social use plants and 1 (0.4%) poisonous.

samples.ref: Àwọn yòókù (24%) jẹ́ àwọn èròjà fún ilé kíkọ́, ṣíṣe àwọn irinṣẹ́ oko, òrùlé ṣíṣe àti okùn ṣíṣe.
samples.hyp: Some of the plants were also used for medicinal purposes.

samples.src: Since the majority of the rural populations reportedly used firewood, 25% of plants were used for that.
samples.ref: Nígbà tí púpọ̀ nínú àwọn èèyàn lábúlé ń lo igi ìdánná, 25% àwọn ewéko ní wọ́n ń lò fun.

samples.src: The researchers said only one (0.4%) plant was mentioned for poisoning purposes.
samples.ref: Àwọn aṣẹ̀wádìí sọ pe ewéko kan soso (0.4%) ni wọ́n sọ pé wọ́n ń lò gẹ́gẹ́ bíi májèlé.

samples.src: They also said the way plants were distributed in the area was influenced by the environment, what people liked to eat, as well as family financial status and business needs.
samples.ref: Wọ́n tún sọ pé bí ìpín àwọn ewéko ní agbègbè náà ń wáyé látàrí ipa àyíká, ohun tí àwọn èèyàn fẹ́ràn láti máa jẹ, ipò àwọn ẹbí kọ̀ọ̀kan àti àwọn ohun tí oko-òwọ̀ wọn nílò.

samples.src: For example, an area called Wenka that had irrigation water and was close to a main town, had many gardens and recorded 130 different plants.
samples.ref: Bí àpẹẹrẹ, agbègbè kan tó ń jẹ́ Wenka tó ni omi ẹ̀rọ, tó sì súnmọ́ ìgboro, ní ọgbà-etíle púpọ̀, wọ́n sì ṣe ìkọsílẹ̀ ewéko oríṣiríṣi tó tó 130.

samples.src: The Wenka people also grew and supplied fruits and vegetables to the town market.
samples.ref: Àwọn ará Wenka sì tún ń gbin, bẹ́ẹ̀ wọ́n ń pèsè àwọn èso àti ẹ̀fọ́ sí ọjà ìgboro.
samples.hyp: They also engaged in animal husbandry, particularly in the rearing of goats and sheep.

samples.src: Lastly, the researchers said most farmers preferred to grow plants that had many uses.
samples.ref: Nígbẹ̀yìn, àwọn aṣèwádìí sọ pé púpọ̀ nínú àwọn àgbẹ̀ fẹ́ràn láti máa gbin àwọn ewéko tó ní ìwúlò púpọ̀.

samples.src: The researchers said their results confirmed that indeed farmers grew a high number of different types of plants in their gardens, and for different uses.
samples.ref: Àwọn aṣèwádìí sọ pé èsì ìwádìí wọn fìdí ẹ̀ múlẹ̀ pé, lóòótọ́ àwọn àgbẹ̀ gbin ewéko oríṣiríṣi tó pọ̀ nínú àwọn ọgbà-etílé wọn, èyí fún ìlò ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀.

samples.src: Even though these researchers found that most farmers grew herbs, others researchers had said trees were more common in the area.
samples.ref: Pẹ̀lú bí àwọn aṣèwádìí ṣe ṣàwárí pé púpọ̀ àwọn àgbẹ̀ ń gbin àwọn egbòogi, àwọn aṣèwádìí míràn ti ní àwọn igi gògòrò ló wọ́pọ̀ jù lọ ní agbègbè náà.

samples.src: The researchers of this study were based in universities in Ethiopia.
